## 1. Wczytywanie danych
```{r}
data <- read.csv("HepatitisCdata.csv") |> select(-X) |> na.omit()
```

## 2. Podstawowa transformacja
### 2.1 Standaryzacja
Standardyzujemy wszystkie zmienne numeryczne (cechy 4:14)
```{r}
data <- data |>
  mutate(across(4:ncol(data), ~ as.vector(scale(.))))

```
### 2.2 Uproszczenie wartości zmiennych kategorycznych
```{r}
data$Category <- sub("=.*", "", data$Category)
```

## 3. Analiza korelacji cech
```{r}
chart.Correlation(data[,4:ncol(data)], histogram=T, pch="+")
``` 

```{r}
sus_data <- data |> filter(Category == "0s")
```

## 4. 
```{r}
chart.Correlation(data[,c("ALB", "ALP", "CHE", "BIL", "CHOL", "GGT", "PROT")], histogram=T, pch="+")
```

```{r}
cor.mat <- data[, 4:ncol(data)] |> cor_mat()
cor.mat |> cor_plot()
```
## 5. Podział na zbiory treningowe i testowe.
### 5.1 Dla Autoencoder:
Wybieramy część **tylko** zdrowych pacjentów.

```{r}
set.seed(42)

data$Sex <- as.factor(data$Sex)
zeros <- which(data$Category == "0")
idx   <- sample(zeros, size = round(0.8 * length(zeros)))

feature_cols <- setdiff(names(data), "Category")

data_Train_AENC <- data[idx, feature_cols]
data_Test_AENC  <- data[-idx, ]

# labels aligned with the test set (1 = anomaly, 0 = healthy)
is_outlier_AENC <- as.integer(data_Test_AENC$Category != "0")
data_Test_AENC  <- data_Test_AENC[, feature_cols]

stopifnot(nrow(data_Test_AENC) == length(is_outlier_AENC))

table(is_outlier_AENC)
summary(data_Train_AENC)
summary(data_Test_AENC)
```

### 5.2 Dla iForest:
Wybieramy część **wszystkich** pacjentów.

```{r}
# train test split, stratify
set.seed(42)
not_sus <- which(data$Category != "0s")
idx   <- sample(not_sus, size = round(0.8 * length(not_sus)))
#idx <- sample(nrow(data), size=round(0.8 * nrow(data)))


data_Train_iFor <- data[idx, feature_cols]
data_Test_iFor_Cat  <- data[-idx, ]          # keep Category for labels
data_Test_iFor  <- data_Test_iFor_Cat[, feature_cols]
is_outlier_iFor <- as.integer(data_Test_iFor$Category != "0")

#stopifnot(nrow(data_Train_iFor) + nrow(data_Test_iFor) == n)
```

## 6. Uczenie lasu losowego 
```{r}
set.seed(42)

iso_forest <- isolation.forest(data_Train_iFor)
scores     <- predict(iso_forest, data_Test_iFor)
avg_depths <- predict(iso_forest, data_Test_iFor, type="avg_depth")
```

Hierachical Clustering

```{r}
scores_df <- data.frame(
  Category = data_Test_iFor_Cat$Category,
  Score    = scores,
  AvgDepth = avg_depths
)

summary(scores_df)

scores_df |> group_by(Category) |> summarize(mean_score = mean(Score), mean_avg_depth = mean(AvgDepth), n = n())
```

```{r}
library(isotree); library(pROC); library(PRROC); library(dplyr)

lab <- data$Category
nz  <- which(lab != "0s")                 # trainable rows
K <- 5; R <- 10
oof <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(data), R)    # out-of-fold scores

for (r in 1:R) {
  set.seed(r)
  # stratify on Category (0 vs 1,2,3) so rare classes spread across folds
  folds <- caret::createFolds(lab[nz], k = K)
  s0s <- numeric(0)
  for (f in folds) {
    tr  <- nz[-f]; te <- nz[f]
    m   <- isolation.forest(data[tr, feature_cols], ntrees = 500, seed = r)
    oof[te, r] <- predict(m, data[te, feature_cols])
    # score 0s with this fold's model too, then average
    s0s <- rbind(s0s, predict(m, data[lab == "0s", feature_cols]))
  }
  oof[lab == "0s", r] <- colMeans(s0s)
}

score <- rowMeans(oof)                    # or evaluate per repeat and report the spread

# Confirmed anomalies (1-3) vs normal (0)
sel <- lab != "0s"
y   <- as.integer(lab[sel] != "0")
roc_obj <- roc(y, score[sel]); ci.auc(roc_obj)
pr.curve(scores.class0 = score[sel][y == 1],
         scores.class1 = score[sel][y == 0], curve = TRUE)
```
